description: We are here to generate a new world
summary:
For the NASA Space Apps Challenge (Challenge 01: Abandoned But Not Forgotten), we created a Space Time Capsule that tells the stories of NASA equipment left on the Moon and Mars. We explain why equipment was left behind: weight, fuel and mission design. Then we explore:

Apollo 11’s descent stage
the laser retroreflector that still helps scientists measure the distance to the Moon
the Mars rovers Sojourner, Spirit and Opportunity

We made it both as a presentation and as an interactive Scratch story with a quiz at the end. Our message: “Every mission leaves something behind — sometimes equipment, always knowledge.”
details:
What does it do / how does it work?
It’s a digital time capsule. Viewers move page by page through the story of each machine: what it did, why it stayed behind, and what it still teaches us. In the Scratch version, NEXT and BACK buttons let you explore at your own pace, and the last page is a quiz.

What benefits does it have?
It shows that “left behind” doesn’t mean useless. Students learn real space history, the science of missions, and how scientists still use these machines and their data today.

What is the intended impact?
We want people to respect and remember these machines as part of space history, and to inspire students to become future explorers and scientists.

What tools did you use?

  • A presentation tool for the slides
    • a page variable
    • broadcasts (NEXT/PREV)
    • “if” blocks to change the backdrop
    • clickable button sprites
  • NASA’s official mission information for our research

How is it creative?
We turned space history into a “time capsule” journey with simple drawings, a quiz and an interactive version people can click through.

What factors did we consider?

  • Accuracy: We used real NASA facts and dates.
  • Clear story order: The question comes first, then the Moon, then Mars, then a quiz.
  • Simple language: Every student can understand it.
  • Design: We used a matching space theme with clear titles.
  • Engaging the audience: The quiz and NEXT/BACK buttons keep the audience involved.
